newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Medis El in breast cancer vaccine pact.
newsitem.headline: Medis El in breast cancer vaccine pact.

text.p: Israel's Medis El Ltd said on Thursday it had entered an agreement with Tel Aviv University to try to develop a vaccine against breast cancer.
Medis El said it would provide funding and its CellScan technology to the project. The amount of the investment will be tied to the achievement of key milestones.
Medis El will receive an equity in any vaccine developed and the exclusive right to use and distribute antigens developed for breast cancer tests.
Robert K. Lifton, chairman of Medis El, said the agreement offered the opportunity to "develop a vaccine against breast cancer from a considerably advanced starting point".
He said in a statement, "Going forward, our strategy will involve seeking opportunities to own an interest in vaccines and drugs whose development is enhanced by the use of the CellScan system."
CellScan is a laser-based cytometer that repeatedly monitors the fluorescent intensity and polarisation of individual living cells such as lymphocytes.
The university team has already reported considerable progress in development of the vaccine, working with mice.

Mice immunised with the vaccine and then injected with cancer-causing cells showed a lower incidence of tumour formation, were tumour-free for longer periods and developed smaller tumours. Initial findings showed that the vaccine prevented or reduced the degree of metastasis, Medis El said.

The researchers will use it to help identify immunogens, an important part of the process of selecting candidates for immunisation. CellScan will also enable the in-vitro use of blood to evaluate the efficacy of the vaccination.
Medis El, founded in 1992, develops and manufactures electronic diagnostic products for the medical and scientific sectors.
